cards.b: A graph showing river discharge over time after a rainstorm, often with rainfall bars.
The time between peak rainfall and peak discharge.
Rising limb: discharge increases after rain. Falling limb: discharge drops back towards base flow.
Short lag time, steep rising limb and high peak discharge. Higher flood risk.
The pattern of a river's discharge over the course of a year.
Intense or prolonged rain, saturated or frozen ground, impermeable rock, steep slopes, snowmelt, monsoon.
Urbanisation, deforestation, building on flood plains, drains that speed up runoff.

cards.f: How does urbanisation increase flood risk?
cards.b: Impermeable surfaces reduce infiltration, drains carry water quickly to the river: shorter lag time, higher peak.
Social: deaths, homelessness, disease. Economic: damage, lost business and crops. Environmental: erosion, pollution, habitat damage.
Dams and reservoirs, embankments, flood walls, channel straightening, relief channels.
Afforestation, flood plain zoning, river restoration, flood warnings and education.
Stores water, reduces flood peaks, gives HEP. But very expensive, floods land upstream, traps sediment.
Planning rules that stop building on flood-prone land. Cheap and effective but does not protect existing homes.
Trees intercept rain and take up water, so less surface runoff reaches the river and lag time lengthens.
Fertiliser runoff adds nutrients, causing algal blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish.
Sewage, industrial waste, and agricultural runoff (fertilisers, pesticides).

cards.f: Rich vs poor country flood impacts
cards.b: Rich: more insurance, better defences, fewer deaths, high costs. Poor: more deaths, slower recovery, weaker defences and housing.

short.q: Describe what a river hydrograph shows.
short.model: It shows how a river's discharge changes over time after a rainstorm, including the rising limb, peak discharge and falling limb.
points: after a storm / rising limb and peak

short.q: Explain how deforestation can increase flood risk.
short.model: Fewer trees means less interception and less water taken up, so more rain reaches the ground as surface runoff and enters the river quickly, giving a higher peak.
points: more surface runoff, shorter lag time

short.q: Give two reasons why some countries suffer more from flooding than others.
short.model: Poorer countries may have fewer flood defences and warning systems. They may also have more people living on flood plains in weak housing, and less money to recover.
points: vulnerable housing or location / slower recovery

short.q: Explain one disadvantage of using soft engineering to manage flooding.
short.model: Soft engineering such as afforestation is slow to take effect and may not be enough to stop floods in extreme rainfall.
points: not enough in severe floods or cannot protect existing homes

short.q: Explain how flood warnings help to reduce the impacts of a flood.
short.model: Warnings based on forecasts and river gauges give people time to move belongings and evacuate, which reduces deaths and damage.
points: gives time to evacuate / move property
